topics.headline: Iranian missiles hit US bases as FOIA data points to 400 American deaths
topics.snippet: An Iranian ballistic missile struck a US base in Jordan overnight, part of a wider surprise attack on American installations in the Middle East. Data obtained through a Freedom of Information Act requ…
topics.text:
iranian missiles hit us bases as foia data points to 400 american deaths
an iranian ballistic missile struck a us base in jordan overnight, part of a wider surprise attack on american installations in the middle east. data obtained through a freedom of information act request to the defense manpower data center indicates more than 400 us service members have died in the conflict with iran. china is reported to be supplying iran with roughly 400 air defense missile launchers valued at $60 million to $70 million. president trump responded by vowing to strike iran far harder, despite earlier statements that his administration wanted to negotiate.

topics.headline: Epstein survivors hand files to senators ahead of Blanche confirmation vote
topics.snippet: More than ten Epstein survivors went office to office on Capitol Hill delivering copies of the Epstein files to senators due to vote on Todd Blanche's confirmation. The group targeted Republican membe…
topics.text:
epstein survivors hand files to senators ahead of blanche confirmation vote
more than ten epstein survivors went office to office on capitol hill delivering copies of the epstein files to senators due to vote on todd blanche's confirmation. the group targeted republican members of the judiciary committee, including katie britt, mike lee, josh hawley and john kennedy, urging them to vote no. organisers said the campaign would continue regardless of whether blanche is confirmed.

topics.headline: Administration to end Medicare Part D subsidies at the end of 2026
topics.snippet: The Trump administration announced overnight that Medicare Part D subsidies will expire at the end of 2026 and will not be available in 2027. The program works with private insurers to lower the cost…
topics.text:
administration to end medicare part d subsidies at the end of 2026
the trump administration announced overnight that medicare part d subsidies will expire at the end of 2026 and will not be available in 2027. the program works with private insurers to lower the cost of brand-name and generic prescriptions for medicare enrollees, most of whom are seniors or people with disabilities. mehmet oz, who heads the centers for medicare and medicaid services, said the subsidies are being cut off at the end of the year.

topics.headline: Thune says Senate lacks votes for SAVE Act or ending the filibuster
topics.snippet: Majority Leader John Thune confirmed that Republicans do not have the votes to pass the SAVE Act or to eliminate the filibuster. Republicans may attempt to move the measure through budget reconciliati…
topics.text:
thune says senate lacks votes for save act or ending the filibuster
majority leader john thune confirmed that republicans do not have the votes to pass the save act or to eliminate the filibuster. republicans may attempt to move the measure through budget reconciliation, but the votes for that route are also not currently there, leaving the bill without a path before the november elections. separately, trump's legal team missed the deadline to seek a supreme court rehearing in his birthright citizenship case, foreclosing that appeal.

topics.headline: CENTCOM warns troops that shared videos could help Iran target US bases
topics.snippet: The top US commander for the Middle East warned service members that videos they post can help Iran assess the effects of its strikes on American bases. Sources said phone restrictions, including conf…
topics.text:
centcom warns troops that shared videos could help iran target us bases
the top us commander for the middle east warned service members that videos they post can help iran assess the effects of its strikes on american bases. sources said phone restrictions, including confiscations, are under consideration.

topics.headline: Iraq's Iran-backed armed network numbers about 50,000 fighters
topics.snippet: Iran-backed armed groups in Iraq comprise roughly 50,000 fighters across about ten hardline factions, according to two security officials cited by Reuters. The network is a significant factor in the r…
topics.text:
iraq's iran-backed armed network numbers about 50,000 fighters
iran-backed armed groups in iraq comprise roughly 50,000 fighters across about ten hardline factions, according to two security officials cited by reuters. the network is a significant factor in the regional conflict involving iran, israel and the united states.

topics.headline: Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment throughout congressional hearing
topics.snippet: Anthony Fauci declined to answer questions at a congressional hearing, citing his Fifth Amendment rights on the advice of counsel. Questions he refused to answer included whether he was made aware of…
topics.text:
fauci invokes fifth amendment throughout congressional hearing
anthony fauci declined to answer questions at a congressional hearing, citing his fifth amendment rights on the advice of counsel. questions he refused to answer included whether he was made aware of gain-of-function research on monkeypox at the national biodefense analysis and countermeasures center and fort detrick, and whether the cia transferred funds to the nih under an interagency agreement. one of his attorneys was ordered removed from the room by the chair after repeatedly speaking while not recognised. lawmakers also pressed him over past remarks about making life difficult for people who declined covid vaccination.

topics.headline: Pentagon AI post shows prompt asking a bot to help generate a war
topics.snippet: A post from the Department of War's official account promoting new AI task forces embedded with the US Pacific Fleet included an image of a service member using an AI assistant. Zooming into the scree…
topics.text:
pentagon ai post shows prompt asking a bot to help generate a war
a post from the department of war's official account promoting new ai task forces embedded with the us pacific fleet included an image of a service member using an ai assistant. zooming into the screenshot shows the typed prompt "i need help building an agent to generate a war." the post drew widespread ridicule online, with critics questioning whether it was deliberate trolling or an operational security lapse.

topics.headline: Russia charges Telegram founder Pavel Durov with aiding terrorism
topics.snippet: Russian authorities have charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov over the platform's alleged use by Ukrainian intelligence services. The FSB said Durov has been placed on an international wanted list.
topics.text:
russia charges telegram founder pavel durov with aiding terrorism
russian authorities have charged telegram founder pavel durov over the platform's alleged use by ukrainian intelligence services. the fsb said durov has been placed on an international wanted list.

topics.headline: Iran launches ballistic missile attack on U.S. forces in the Middle East
topics.snippet: U.S. Central Command said Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces launched multiple ballistic missiles from Iran at 5:45 p.m. ET on July 28 in what it described as an attempted surprise attack on U.S…
topics.text:
iran launches ballistic missile attack on u.s. forces in the middle east
u.s. central command said islamic revolutionary guard corps forces launched multiple ballistic missiles from iran at 5:45 p.m. et on july 28 in what it described as an attempted surprise attack on u.s. bases in the middle east. centcom said all of the missiles were intercepted and that u.s. forces remain at a high state of readiness.

topics.headline: Netanyahu and Zelensky visit Washington as Iran and Ukraine wars escalate
topics.snippet: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky both travelled to Washington on July 28, with the White House indicating Trump would meet each leader separately ra…
topics.text:
netanyahu and zelensky visit washington as iran and ukraine wars escalate
israeli prime minister benjamin netanyahu and ukrainian president volodymyr zelensky both travelled to washington on july 28, with the white house indicating trump would meet each leader separately rather than jointly. both leaders also attended the funeral of senator lindsey graham, who had recently returned from a trip to ukraine before his death and was a leading republican supporter of kyiv. netanyahu, who is subject to an international criminal court arrest warrant, was photographed at the funeral alongside secretary of state marco rubio and pete hegseth, and sean hannity's eulogy focused heavily on graham's support for israel. ukraine also confirmed it deliberately struck iranian vessels over the weekend.

topics.headline: Gulf states back Omani plan for voluntary Iranian fees in Strait of Hormuz
topics.snippet: Gulf states have endorsed an Omani proposal under which Iran would collect voluntary fees for passage through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a source cited by Reuters. Roughly one in five barrels…
topics.text:
gulf states back omani plan for voluntary iranian fees in strait of hormuz
gulf states have endorsed an omani proposal under which iran would collect voluntary fees for passage through the strait of hormuz, according to a source cited by reuters. roughly one in five barrels of the world's oil consumption normally transits the strait.

topics.headline: Expanding yellow line in Gaza forces families to move again
topics.snippet: Residents of Gaza say the advancing yellow line is displacing families who have already been forced to relocate. The shifting boundary is pushing people into new areas as the conflict continues.
topics.text:
expanding yellow line in gaza forces families to move again
residents of gaza say the advancing yellow line is displacing families who have already been forced to relocate. the shifting boundary is pushing people into new areas as the conflict continues.

topics.headline: ICE used forced medical treatment on immigration detainee during hunger strike
topics.snippet: A document released by ICE and reviewed by the Guardian shows the agency subjected at least one detainee on hunger strike to forcible medical treatment, including forced feeding, hydration, forced uri…
topics.text:
ice used forced medical treatment on immigration detainee during hunger strike
a document released by ice and reviewed by the guardian shows the agency subjected at least one detainee on hunger strike to forcible medical treatment, including forced feeding, hydration, forced urinary catheterization or involuntary blood draws. the detainee began the hunger strike between october and december of last year. international human rights groups have described such forced treatment as tantamount to torture, and it can carry serious medical complications.

topics.headline: Migrant children agency data led to more than 12,000 arrests
topics.snippet: More than 12,000 people were arrested after the U.S. agency responsible for unaccompanied child migrants shared leads with Immigration and Customs Enforcement, according to a Reuters investigation. Th…
topics.text:
migrant children agency data led to more than 12,000 arrests
more than 12,000 people were arrested after the u.s. agency responsible for unaccompanied child migrants shared leads with immigration and customs enforcement, according to a reuters investigation. the data sharing linked information gathered through the child migrant program to enforcement operations.

topics.headline: ICE steps up arrests of travellers with expired visas at U.S. airports
topics.snippet: ICE is escalating stops and arrests at airports, targeting people travelling domestically who have overstayed their visas, according to the New York Times. Cooperation of this kind between TSA and ICE…
topics.text:
ice steps up arrests of travellers with expired visas at u.s. airports
ice is escalating stops and arrests at airports, targeting people travelling domestically who have overstayed their visas, according to the new york times. cooperation of this kind between tsa and ice previously did not exist, and the practice has already occurred on at least a dozen occasions. those affected include people awaiting green cards or visa extensions, who were rarely detained at airports in the past.

topics.headline: Texas police searched 83,000 Flock cameras nationwide in abortion investigation
topics.snippet: Texas authorities queried roughly 83,000 Flock license plate cameras across the country in April 2025 while searching for a woman a sheriff said had self-administered an abortion, according to 404 Med…
topics.text:
texas police searched 83,000 flock cameras nationwide in abortion investigation
texas authorities queried roughly 83,000 flock license plate cameras across the country in april 2025 while searching for a woman a sheriff said had self-administered an abortion, according to 404 media. the searches included states where abortion is legal, such as washington and illinois. no charges resulted, but experts say the case shows officers in states with abortion bans can search camera networks in states where the procedure is legal.

topics.headline: Bureau of Land Management approves first data center on federal public land
topics.snippet: The Bureau of Land Management approved converting a 2023 solar and battery storage permit in Boulder City, Nevada into a data center, on the reasoning that the two uses are "substantially the same." T…
topics.text:
bureau of land management approves first data center on federal public land
the bureau of land management approved converting a 2023 solar and battery storage permit in boulder city, nevada into a data center, on the reasoning that the two uses are "substantially the same." the switch was approved with no new environmental review and no public comment period, and the nearby city learned of it afterward. it is the first data center approved on blm-managed land, and the pentagon is separately leasing military land to private data center developers in texas and utah. a bill to ban data centers on federal land has been introduced, and a petition asks interior to rescind the approval.

topics.headline: Great Salt Lake near dry as water diversions continue
topics.snippet: The Great Salt Lake is all but dried up and toxic dust is blowing across northern Utah, while 62% of the water that would otherwise refill the lake is diverted for human use. Of that diverted water, 7…
topics.text:
great salt lake near dry as water diversions continue
the great salt lake is all but dried up and toxic dust is blowing across northern utah, while 62% of the water that would otherwise refill the lake is diverted for human use. of that diverted water, 71% goes to agriculture and 81% of the agricultural share grows hay and alfalfa, crops that account for less than 1% of utah's gdp, with an estimated third to half exported, mainly to china. governor spencer cox, an alfalfa farm owner, recently appointed farmer hannah freese as great salt lake commissioner to coordinate rescue, conservation and policy plans.

topics.headline: Inver Grove Heights council meeting erupts over data center variance
topics.snippet: An Inver Grove Heights City Council meeting descended into shouting ahead of a discussion on data centers, with residents objecting that no community input or public comment was required before approv…
topics.text:
inver grove heights council meeting erupts over data center variance
an inver grove heights city council meeting descended into shouting ahead of a discussion on data centers, with residents objecting that no community input or public comment was required before approving a variance. the mayor walked out of the meeting without answering questions.

topics.headline: Beshear presses McConnell to explain Senate absence or resign
topics.snippet: Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear sent a follow-up letter to Senator Mitch McConnell demanding he either disclose the nature of his health issues or resign, according to a copy obtained by CNN. The lette…
topics.text:
beshear presses mcconnell to explain senate absence or resign
kentucky governor andy beshear sent a follow-up letter to senator mitch mcconnell demanding he either disclose the nature of his health issues or resign, according to a copy obtained by cnn. the letter says beshear is writing on the assumption mcconnell is capable of reading and responding and is not incapacitated in consciousness or cognition, and the daily beast reported it was also sent to senate republican leader john thune. beshear has no power as governor to compel a resignation.

topics.headline: Trump's age and health draw scrutiny after Graham's death
topics.snippet: The Washington Post reports that Trump has been discussing his own mortality more often behind the scenes since Lindsey Graham's sudden death, and has looked into Graham's family history for genetic f…
topics.text:
trump's age and health draw scrutiny after graham's death
the washington post reports that trump has been discussing his own mortality more often behind the scenes since lindsey graham's sudden death, and has looked into graham's family history for genetic factors while speculating that graham's travel schedule contributed to his declining health. at 80, trump is the oldest president in u.s. history with two years left in his term. during graham's funeral he appeared to struggle to stay awake, with observers describing periods of several minutes in which he seemed asleep.

topics.headline: U.S. drone production trails far behind Ukraine's output
topics.snippet: Ukraine is projected to produce roughly 500,000 drones per month, while cumulative Pentagon program orders stood below 200,000 as of February. The Pentagon is pushing to build a domestic drone supply…
topics.text:
u.s. drone production trails far behind ukraine's output
ukraine is projected to produce roughly 500,000 drones per month, while cumulative pentagon program orders stood below 200,000 as of february. the pentagon is pushing to build a domestic drone supply chain to close the gap.

topics.headline: Kremlin monitoring Wildberries after Ukrainian drone strikes on warehouses
topics.snippet: Russia's government is monitoring the retailer Wildberries after Ukrainian drone attacks hit eight warehouses, affecting more than 10% of its storage capacity since July 18. No decision on state aid h…
topics.text:
kremlin monitoring wildberries after ukrainian drone strikes on warehouses
russia's government is monitoring the retailer wildberries after ukrainian drone attacks hit eight warehouses, affecting more than 10% of its storage capacity since july 18. no decision on state aid has been made.

topics.snippet: Officials say the administration is preparing import bans covering new models of Chinese-made robots and inverters. The measures are framed as a technology security step.

trump administration moves to block new chinese robots and inverters
officials say the administration is preparing import bans covering new models of chinese-made robots and inverters. the measures are framed as a technology security step.

topics.headline: Bipartisan House bill would direct State Department to counter North Korean activity
topics.snippet: House Resolution 9963, introduced on July 27, would authorize the Secretary of State to coordinate with U.S. allies and partners to detect, attribute and disrupt certain North Korean activities. It is…
topics.text:
bipartisan house bill would direct state department to counter north korean activity
house resolution 9963, introduced on july 27, would authorize the secretary of state to coordinate with u.s. allies and partners to detect, attribute and disrupt certain north korean activities. it is sponsored by representative young kim of california's 40th district and co-sponsored by democrat ami bera of california's 6th district, and has been referred to the foreign affairs committee. this congress has passed only an estimated 1% to 3% of introduced bills.

topics.headline: Former Navy SEAL sentenced for plot to bomb San Diego protest
topics.snippet: Gregory Vandenberg, 49, a former Navy SEAL, was convicted and sentenced to 16 months in federal prison for plotting to attack a No Kings protest in San Diego with explosives.
topics.text:
former navy seal sentenced for plot to bomb san diego protest
gregory vandenberg, 49, a former navy seal, was convicted and sentenced to 16 months in federal prison for plotting to attack a no kings protest in san diego with explosives.

topics.headline: Berlin Pride attack suspect recorded pledge to Islamic State, prosecutors say
topics.snippet: German prosecutors say the suspect in the attack on Berlin Pride recorded a pledge of allegiance to the Islamic State. The finding ties the case to the group as the investigation proceeds.
topics.text:
berlin pride attack suspect recorded pledge to islamic state, prosecutors say
german prosecutors say the suspect in the attack on berlin pride recorded a pledge of allegiance to the islamic state. the finding ties the case to the group as the investigation proceeds.

topics.snippet: Representative Thomas Massie said the Israeli lobby spent $30 million to defeat him, and claimed a generation is now aware of what he called its corrosive influence on the U.S. government. He said eve…
topics.text:
massie says israeli lobby spent $30 million against his campaign
representative thomas massie said the israeli lobby spent $30 million to defeat him, and claimed a generation is now aware of what he called its corrosive influence on the u.s. government. he said every other elected republican in congress is bought, captured or intimidated to some degree.

topics.headline: Canadian travel boycott costs U.S. more than $3 billion
topics.snippet: A new Canadian government report shows the United States has lost more than $3 billion in revenue as Canadians curtail travel south of the border, with July visits down 30% year over year. It is the s…
topics.text:
canadian travel boycott costs u.s. more than $3 billion
a new canadian government report shows the united states has lost more than $3 billion in revenue as canadians curtail travel south of the border, with july visits down 30% year over year. it is the steepest such decline since 2001. cited causes include tariffs on canada and other actions by the trump administration.

topics.headline: AI firms buying and shredding rare books to train models
topics.snippet: AI companies are bulk buying rare and antique books, cutting off the spines to scan them at high speed and then shredding the originals, according to reporting by Futurism and 404 Media. A federal jud…
topics.text:
ai firms buying and shredding rare books to train models
ai companies are bulk buying rare and antique books, cutting off the spines to scan them at high speed and then shredding the originals, according to reporting by futurism and 404 media. a federal judge has ruled the practice qualifies as fair use because destroying the original keeps only one copy in existence at a time. no one in the pipeline verifies whether a book is the last surviving copy, and local histories and self-published war memoirs are among the material being destroyed.

topics.headline: FIFA plans $20 billion Kushner-backed company to run the World Cup
topics.snippet: FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced a plan to create a $20 billion private company, backed by the Kushner family alongside other private investors, to run the World Cup. UEFA objected, saying fo…
topics.text:
fifa plans $20 billion kushner-backed company to run the world cup
fifa president gianni infantino announced a plan to create a $20 billion private company, backed by the kushner family alongside other private investors, to run the world cup. uefa objected, saying football is not fifa's to sell and that no one owns the game. the plan was first reported by the financial times; trump has separately said he wants to appoint infantino as un secretary general.

topics.headline: Federal survey finds daily marijuana use now exceeds alcohol and cigarettes
topics.snippet: The National Survey on Drug Use and Health, released this week, found about 21.4 million Americans aged 12 and over report using marijuana daily or near-daily, defined as more than 20 times in a 30-da…
topics.text:
federal survey finds daily marijuana use now exceeds alcohol and cigarettes
the national survey on drug use and health, released this week, found about 21.4 million americans aged 12 and over report using marijuana daily or near-daily, defined as more than 20 times in a 30-day period. that compares with 17.2 million for alcohol and 19.9 million for cigarettes. it is the first time marijuana has topped both in daily use.

topics.headline: Iran says it will hold fire while US bombing pause continues
topics.snippet: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran will halt its attacks for as long as the US bombing pause remains in place, after both sides held fire for two days. Tehran remains skeptical that the…
topics.text:
iran says it will hold fire while us bombing pause continues
a senior iranian official told reuters that iran will halt its attacks for as long as the us bombing pause remains in place, after both sides held fire for two days. tehran remains skeptical that the pause will hold. drone attacks reported across saudi arabia, jordan and iraq are testing the pause, and the source of some of the drones remains unclear.

topics.headline: Iran blames Ukraine for strike on commercial vessel as conflicts converge
topics.snippet: Iran's foreign minister accused President Zelensky and Ukraine of attacking an Iranian commercial vessel and killing an Iranian sailor, saying the strike was carried out on Israel's behalf to draw Eur…
topics.text:
iran blames ukraine for strike on commercial vessel as conflicts converge
iran's foreign minister accused president zelensky and ukraine of attacking an iranian commercial vessel and killing an iranian sailor, saying the strike was carried out on israel's behalf to draw europe into a wider war. ukraine has been described as confirming the strike on iranian vessels was deliberate. the development raises the prospect of the russia-ukraine war and the us-israel conflict with iran merging into a single broader conflict involving yemen and gulf states.

topics.headline: Netanyahu and Zelensky head to Washington for separate Trump meetings and Graham funeral
topics.snippet: Benjamin Netanyahu, who is subject to an International Criminal Court arrest warrant, traveled to Washington to be received by President Trump, alongside a visit by Volodymyr Zelensky. The White House…
topics.text:
netanyahu and zelensky head to washington for separate trump meetings and graham funeral
benjamin netanyahu, who is subject to an international criminal court arrest warrant, traveled to washington to be received by president trump, alongside a visit by volodymyr zelensky. the white house says the two leaders will meet trump separately rather than together, and both are also attending the funeral of senator lindsey graham, who died shortly after returning from a trip to ukraine. the icc cannot act against netanyahu on us soil because the rome statute was signed by bill clinton without congressional ratification and later unsigned by george w. bush. commentary also highlighted the scale of us financial support for israel, put at roughly $17.47 billion a year across the states.

topics.headline: Trump calls heckler a communist after Epstein taunt at rally
topics.snippet: At a rally focused on his tariff policy, President Trump was heckled by a man shouting that he is a "pedophile protector." Trump did not address the substance of the accusation and instead called the…
topics.text:
trump calls heckler a communist after epstein taunt at rally
at a rally focused on his tariff policy, president trump was heckled by a man shouting that he is a "pedophile protector." trump did not address the substance of the accusation and instead called the heckler a communist. the exchange came amid continued pressure over the administration's failure to release the epstein files.

topics.headline: Court filings accuse Rep. Max Miller of assaulting wife and injuring toddler
topics.snippet: New court filings reported by Mother Jones allege that Representative Max Miller, a Republican from Ohio, threw hot water at his wife, shoved her and held a gun to her head. His wife, Emily Moreno, a…
topics.text:
court filings accuse rep. max miller of assaulting wife and injuring toddler
new court filings reported by mother jones allege that representative max miller, a republican from ohio, threw hot water at his wife, shoved her and held a gun to her head. his wife, emily moreno, a policy adviser and daughter of ohio senator bernie moreno, told detectives she could not rule out that miller caused a fracture to their two-year-old daughter's collarbone. child protection specialists reviewing the case described bruising near the fracture as resembling a handprint.

topics.headline: Judge orders Trump trust to open financial records to BBC
topics.snippet: A federal magistrate judge in South Florida entered an order requiring the revocable trust that controls President Trump's business operations to turn over financial records to the BBC. The order stem…
topics.text:
judge orders trump trust to open financial records to bbc
a federal magistrate judge in south florida entered an order requiring the revocable trust that controls president trump's business operations to turn over financial records to the bbc. the order stems from trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the broadcaster, in which he alleged significant financial harm. that claim opened the door for the bbc to seek his financials to test the asserted damages. an appeal is considered likely.

topics.headline: Beshear tells McConnell to explain his health or resign as new image released
topics.snippet: Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear sent a follow-up letter to Senator Mitch McConnell demanding an explanation of his health issues or his resignation, addressing it on the assumption McConnell is not inc…
topics.text:
beshear tells mcconnell to explain his health or resign as new image released
kentucky governor andy beshear sent a follow-up letter to senator mitch mcconnell demanding an explanation of his health issues or his resignation, addressing it on the assumption mcconnell is not incapacitated in consciousness or cognition; the letter was also sent to senate republican leader john thune. mcconnell's office released a second image of the senator with his wife elaine chao, this one without a newspaper, and his physician said he continues recovering from a june fall at home. the statement said mcconnell has been discharged from hospital care to a rehabilitation facility and is not yet medically cleared to return to the office. he will not attend the fancy farm political event in kentucky this weekend.

topics.headline: Federal government approves first data center on BLM public land
topics.snippet: The Bureau of Land Management approved a data center in Boulder City, Nevada, by allowing a developer to convert a 2023 permit for solar and battery storage, on the reasoning that the two uses are "su…
topics.text:
federal government approves first data center on blm public land
the bureau of land management approved a data center in boulder city, nevada, by allowing a developer to convert a 2023 permit for solar and battery storage, on the reasoning that the two uses are "substantially the same." the switch was approved with no new environmental review and no public comment period, and the city learned of it afterward. it is the first data center approved on blm-managed land, and a similar pattern has been seen in utah, where a military land designation removed the decision from county control. the pentagon is also leasing military land to private data center developers in texas and utah, and a bill to ban data centers on federal land has been introduced.

topics.headline: Data centers linked to grid flicker across eastern United States
topics.snippet: Electricity flickered on and off for roughly 10 minutes across the eastern United States, from Chicago to Boston to Miami, on July 22. Experts told NBC4 Washington that data centers in Loudoun County,…
topics.text:
data centers linked to grid flicker across eastern united states
electricity flickered on and off for roughly 10 minutes across the eastern united states, from chicago to boston to miami, on july 22. experts told nbc4 washington that data centers in loudoun county, virginia, including the concentration in ashburn known as data center alley, are linked to emerging cracks in the power grid. millions of homes and businesses experienced the disruption, and further strain is expected as more data centers are built.

topics.headline: Republican strategists urge candidates to distance themselves from Trump
topics.snippet: A report from MSNOW says senior Republicans are advising incumbents and challengers to distance themselves from President Trump on the campaign trail ahead of November, arguing that running on the Tru…
topics.text:
republican strategists urge candidates to distance themselves from trump
a report from msnow says senior republicans are advising incumbents and challengers to distance themselves from president trump on the campaign trail ahead of november, arguing that running on the trump agenda will cost them their races. trump's standing has weakened particularly over the war in iran. the advice follows a weekend in which the president posted ai-generated memes on truth social.

topics.headline: Six mass shootings in 48 hours as Seattle festival attack kills three
topics.snippet: Three people were killed and several others wounded, including a toddler, in a shooting at the Bite of Seattle food festival, and one suspect is in custody. Over the preceding 48 hours the United Stat…
topics.text:
six mass shootings in 48 hours as seattle festival attack kills three
three people were killed and several others wounded, including a toddler, in a shooting at the bite of seattle food festival, and one suspect is in custody. over the preceding 48 hours the united states recorded six mass shootings, including incidents in memphis, north charleston, coyote creek and san francisco that killed two more people and injured more than a dozen. the seattle attack was counted as the country's 271st mass shooting of 2026.

topics.headline: Drone attack on Zaporizhzhia holiday camp kills 12
topics.snippet: A drone attack on a holiday camp in Zaporizhzhia killed 12 people, including children. Russian-installed officials blamed Ukraine for the strike. Kyiv had not responded.
topics.text:
drone attack on zaporizhzhia holiday camp kills 12
a drone attack on a holiday camp in zaporizhzhia killed 12 people, including children. russian-installed officials blamed ukraine for the strike. kyiv had not responded.

topics.headline: Ukraine targets 2027 prototype for Freyja missile defense system
topics.snippet: Ukraine is aiming for a mid-2027 prototype of the European Freyja missile-defense system. The system is designed as a lower-cost, open-architecture alternative to the Patriot.
topics.text:
ukraine targets 2027 prototype for freyja missile defense system
ukraine is aiming for a mid-2027 prototype of the european freyja missile-defense system. the system is designed as a lower-cost, open-architecture alternative to the patriot.

topics.snippet: Oil prices declined as markets responded to the fragile pause in US-Iran strikes. New attacks in the region kept risk levels elevated.

oil prices declined as markets responded to the fragile pause in us-iran strikes. new attacks in the region kept risk levels elevated.

topics.snippet: Abdul Ballout, the suspect in the attack on Berlin Pride, was shot dead by police following a nationwide manhunt.
topics.text:
berlin pride attack suspect shot dead by police
abdul ballout, the suspect in the attack on berlin pride, was shot dead by police following a nationwide manhunt.
